- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, it often overcorrects; cap forecast peak at 1–2% above recent high.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overestimates 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply downward bias of 1–3% to mid-range forecasts.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum (e.g., 77+), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to slightly below recent peak.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33), model often lags; forecast should adjust 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model consistently exceeds true outcome by 2–4% over 3–5 consecutive days, apply a 1–2% downward correction to avoid overconfidence bias.
